title: President Ernesto Geisel closes the National Congress of Brazil to control presidential succession as conflict erupts between him, the duristas, Congress, the Church, and the media.
text: Ernesto Beckmann Geiselmɐ̃ ˈɡajzew], German pronunciation: ; 3 August 1907 – 12 September 1996) was a Brazilian Army officer and politician, who served as the 29th president of Brazil from 1974 to 1979, during the Brazilian military dictatorship. Born to German Lutheran immigrants, Geisel attended military prep schools from an early age.

title: In a second ballot by 226 votes in favor and 159 against; the National Congress of Brazil approves a constitutional amendment by Senators Nelson Carneiro and Acioli Filho, that legalizes divorce.
text: Nelson de Souza Carneiro was a Brazilian journalist and politician who had a long career in the federal legislature since the late 1940s, representing various states. He became known for his defense of the right to divorce, which became law in 1977.

title: Writer Rachel de Queiroz becomes the first woman elected to the Brazilian Academy of Letters.
text: Rachel de Queiroz was a Brazilian author, translator and journalist.

title: Jorge Amado's novel Tieta do Agreste is published, which becomes one of his best-selling works.
text: Jorge Leal Amado de Faria, known as Jorge Amado, was a Brazilian writer of the modernist school. He remains the best-known of modern Brazilian writers, with his work having been translated into some 49 languages and popularized in film, including Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands in 1976, and having been nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature at least seven times.

title: Pelé, playing for the New York Cosmos, scores his last goal to defeat Santos FC 2-1, at Giants Stadium, in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States. This would be his last official game, thus saying goodbye to his professional football…
text: Edson Arantes do Nascimento, better known by his nickname Pelé, was a Brazilian professional footballer who played as a forward. Widely regarded as one of the greatest players in history, he was among the most successful and popular sports figures of the 20th century.
